ogTitle: Everett Tile Installation — Built From the Membrane Up
ogDesc: Showers and floors for Everett's craftsman-to-split-level housing stock: bonded waterproofing, a photographed 24-hour flood test, and a straight answer on repair versus re-tile. Call (425) 595-1079.

roles.heroLead: The tile you can see was never the waterproofing — the membrane under it does that job. In an Everett house, 1910s craftsman or 90s split-level, that hidden layer decides whether a shower runs twenty years or ends in a $40,000 framing repair. The assembly gets built, flood-tested for 24 hours and photographed — only then does tile go on.
roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Everett, WA?
roles.costP1: Around Everett the going installed rate is $14–$26 per square foot, with setting materials, substrate prep, tile and labor rolled into one number — the labor line begins near $11/sq ft. Tub-shower surrounds commonly price from $3,200 up to $6,800; give a complete bathroom — floor, shower, niche — a working budget of $6,500–$14,000.
roles.costP2: Here's the part that surprises people: the shape of the tile moves your bill more than its price tag. A $12 large-format porcelain plank can go in cheaper than a $4 mosaic sheet, because you pay for cuts and grout lines, not for the receipt.
roles.costNote: Installed Everett pricing, August 2026 vintage: tile plus materials plus labor. Your free estimate ends in a written quote, and that's the figure to believe.
roles.layersLead: Seven layers sit between your framing and your grout, and every failed shower we open up in Everett is missing at least one — usually the membrane, skipped to save a few hundred dollars on day one and costing thousands to put right later.
roles.whyP1: No leak announces itself. Past the grout it goes, deep into the substrate, and after a couple of winters the evidence appears — hallway floor turned spongy, brown ring blooming on the ceiling below. From there the purchase isn't tile: it's drywall, subfloor, framing and a shower built twice.
roles.whyP2: Waterproofing takes up barely a tenth of a shower's price, yet no other line in the remodel costs so much to leave out.
roles.scopeIntro: Opening prices only — substrate condition, layout and format will move each of them. Once we're on site, the true figure goes down in writing, free.
roles.cardShower: First the pre-slope, then bonded membrane and a passed flood test; after that come niche, entry — curbed or curbless — and the tile. Most of the money goes behind the wall — exactly where it belongs.
roles.cardFloors: Basements, entries, kitchens, mudrooms and bathrooms alike. We true the subfloor before setting anything, adding an uncoupling membrane wherever heat or movement calls for it.
roles.cardBacksplash: Herringbone, subway, mosaic sheet or slab-look porcelain — with clean outlet cuts, finished edge trim, and grout picked to suit the counter rather than the tile carton.
roles.cardHeated: Radiant electric mat on an uncoupling membrane, resistance-checked before and after tile goes down, wired to a dedicated circuit. Makes sense only while the floor is already open.
roles.cardRepair: Cracked field tile, corners opening up, grout past saving. We'll give it to you straight — either a repair holds here, or the substrate below is finished.
roles.cardDemo: Out come old tile, thinset and backer — sheeting and negative air keeping dust contained — and everything leaves on our truck. No pile lands in your driveway.
roles.materialsLead: What goes wrong with tile in Everett is rarely the tile itself — it's a good product set where it doesn't belong. Here's the condensed form of the talk we'd give you in person.
roles.materialsNote: Material pricing only — the install is its own line. We carry samples and tell you flat out which ones earn their cost.
roles.estIntro: Our estimator's on-site arithmetic — square footage, scope, prep and format — reproduced here in rough form. Call it a planning figure rather than a quote.
roles.daysLead: A typical Everett bathroom takes four to six working days. Two of those days surprise people — and they're the two that keep the shower tight.
roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Everett, WA?
roles.faqA1: $14 at the low end, $26 at the high — that's Everett's installed per-square-foot picture, wrapping tile and labor plus substrate prep and setting materials, and labor starts from $11 per square foot on its own. A tub-shower surround normally comes in from $3,200 to $6,800; whole bathrooms — floor, shower and niche included — tend to span $6,500 to $14,000. More than price, format decides the labor: mosaics and large-format both eat clearly more hours per square foot than basic 12×12.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in Everett?
roles.faqA2: Budget an Everett alcove shower somewhere from $3,200 through $6,800 — a figure that already holds demolition, bonded waterproofing, a base or pan with slope, tile, niche and grout. Full-height stone, steam, benches and curbless entries climb past it. The waterproofing share is near one tenth of the cost, and its whole purpose is preventing the repair that runs to tens of thousands.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Always. Behind every shower we set there's a bonded waterproofing system — not bare cement board with thinset over it. The base is pre-sloped, a sheet or liquid membrane runs up the walls, every corner, seam and pipe penetration gets sealed, and a documented 24-hour flood test happens before any tile does. Grout and tile only shed water; the membrane is what actually keeps it out of your framing.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: An Everett bathroom generally takes four to six working days: day one for demo and dust protection, then the substrate-and-waterproofing stage with its 24-hour flood test, followed by a day or two of setting, and last the grout, silicone and trim. Hold off on the first shower for another 24 hours of cure. On its own, a floor is a one-to-two-day affair.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: Porcelain, anywhere water lands or feet do: denser material, chips rarely, absorption under 0.5%. For backsplashes and wall work, ceramic performs well at a lower price. The Everett formula stays simple — every floor and shower floor in porcelain, walls open to ceramic or glass.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes — through an Everett winter it pays for itself in comfort. Call it $11 to $16 per square foot — install and thermostat both in the number — for electric radiant under tile; it's affordable exactly because the floor is already torn up. The system rides an uncoupling membrane, has its resistance read on both sides of the tile work, and needs its own dedicated circuit.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Yes, as a rule. Around $3.50 per square foot handles demo and haul-away, and removing the old floor gives the only honest view of what's beneath — old leaks, rot, movement — while keeping the new height honest at doorways. Over-tiling a flat, well-bonded, sound floor is sometimes possible, but Everett's older houses usually hide something worth discovering, and demo is when you want to find it — not after grout.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Everett?
roles.faqA8: A 30-square-foot Everett backsplash typically installs in the $1,100–$2,200 window — outlets cut in cleanly, edges trimmed, grout color-matched. Herringbone patterns, mosaic sheets, framed range details and full-height slab-look porcelain occupy the upper end; you're buying layout and cutting hours there, not better tile.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Frequently — and telling you which is which is half our job in Everett. Repair and regrout work starts at $8 per square foot: the right call when grout has stained or crumbled, a dropped pan cracked one or two tiles, or the shower corners want old grout swapped for silicone. But hollow-sounding tile, tiles releasing in a pattern, or a wall with any give means the substrate has already failed, and a patch only buys months. We say which one you have before the quote, not after.
roles.faqQ10: Which Everett neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: All of Everett is in range — Riverside, Delta, Bayside, Port Gardner, Rucker Hill, Northwest Everett, Lowell, View Ridge-Madison, Evergreen, Glacier View, Pinehurst, Silver Lake, Westmont, Boulevard Bluffs, Cascade View and Holly — along with Marysville, Mukilteo, Lake Stevens, Snohomish, Mill Creek and the rest of Snohomish County down into King County.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: Every tile job here carries OC Flooring's 2-year workmanship warranty — double the carpet term, because tile's failures show in the second year where carpet's show in the second week. Install a full factory waterproofing assembly and the maker's system warranty rides along on top. And because membrane and flood test are both photographed, the proof follows the house to its next owner.
